panels.title: How to read this dashboard
panels.description: Resource samples describe the model process or benchmark Linux node as named. Sampling may miss short spikes, and the load generator shares the node. Physical-host sensors may be hidden by Lima. Missing telemetry is unavailable, not zero. **Current samples** update during measurement; aggregate peaks/costs update provisionally, then finalize. After a case ends, current-sample series stop; final aggregates remain. Some statistics include earlier server cases (notably lifetime RSS).

options.content: Resource samples describe the model process or benchmark Linux node as named. Sampling may miss short spikes, and the load generator shares the node. Physical-host sensors may be hidden by Lima. Missing telemetry is unavailable, not zero. **Current samples** update during measurement; aggregate peaks/costs update provisionally, then finalize. Process observation spans cases and ends when the model exits. After the one-minute cooldown, node collection stops and final snapshots remain. Some statistics include earlier server cases (notably lifetime RSS). Resource observation starts before warmup, spans stage transitions and continues after completion for one minute after measurement. Final model results remain fixed; node resources keep updating. The CLI opens a start-anchored time range, preserved by dashboard links.

panels.title: Current resident and proportional memory
panels.description: RSS is process memory currently resident in RAM; PSS apportions shared pages. Compare with node headroom for deployment fit. Neither equals model file size or total VM memory. Values are provisional while the case is measuring; final when its phase is final. Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

targets.expr: ((modelgauge_live_value{case="(process)",measurement=~"resource_current_process_(rss|pss)_bytes"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{case="(process)",measurement=~"resource_current_process_(rss|pss)_bytes"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) and (timestamp((modelgauge_live_value{case="(process)",measurement=~"resource_current_process_(rss|pss)_bytes"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{case="(process)",measurement=~"resource_current_process_(rss|pss)_bytes"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) <= scalar(modelgauge_live_window_end_seconds @ end()))

Use headroom rather than treating the observed maximum as a guaranteed limit. Values are provisional while the case is measuring; final when its phase is final. Missing data means not measured yet or unavailable, not zero. Stage/case labels distinguish observations from different workloads. panels.description: Readability/hardware/runtime limitations seen during observation. Missing VM sensors are expected. No measurement is fabricated for unsupported hardware; availability notes do not indicate benchmark failure.

targets.expr: modelgauge_live_unavailable{stage=~"$stage",case=~"$case"}

panels.title: Current model-process CPU
panels.description: CPU time consumed between process observations divided by elapsed wall time, times 100. About 200% represents two cores. Covers warmup and measured work and ends when the owned process exits; missing before a second sample is not zero. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

targets.expr: ((modelgauge_live_value{case="(process)",measurement="resource_current_process_cpu_percent"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{case="(process)",measurement="resource_current_process_cpu_percent"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) and (timestamp((modelgauge_live_value{case="(process)",measurement="resource_current_process_cpu_percent"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{case="(process)",measurement="resource_current_process_cpu_percent"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) <= scalar(modelgauge_live_window_end_seconds @ end()))

panels.title: Benchmark-node CPU across the session
panels.description: Linux guest non-idle/non-iowait CPU percentage across all CPUs between samples. Covers warmup, stage transitions and post-benchmark observation. Not model-only attribution; values continue after the model exits until observation stops. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

targets.expr: ((modelgauge_live_value{case="(node)",measurement="resource_current_node_cpu_usage_percent"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{case="(node)",measurement="resource_current_node_cpu_usage_percent"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) and (timestamp((modelgauge_live_value{case="(node)",measurement="resource_current_node_cpu_usage_percent"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{case="(node)",measurement="resource_current_node_cpu_usage_percent"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) <= scalar(modelgauge_live_window_end_seconds @ end()))

panels.title: Benchmark-node disk available
panels.description: Space available on the benchmark Linux node root filesystem, observed throughout the session. Useful for model/evidence capacity planning, not a disk performance benchmark. After cooldown, this graph is capped at the collection end; it does not invent new samples from held final values.

targets.expr: ((modelgauge_live_value{case="(node)",measurement="resource_current_node_disk_available_bytes"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{case="(node)",measurement="resource_current_node_disk_available_bytes"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) and (timestamp((modelgauge_live_value{case="(node)",measurement="resource_current_node_disk_available_bytes"}) and (timestamp(modelgauge_live_value{case="(node)",measurement="resource_current_node_disk_available_bytes"}) >= scalar(modelgauge_live_started_seconds @ end()))) <= scalar(modelgauge_live_window_end_seconds @ end()))
